title: Can It Drive There: Slope and Roughness From a Height Map, Judged Against What This Vehicle's Motors, Tyres and Wheels Can Do

questions.question: Which two properties of the ground does a height map give?
questions.explanation: They are different: a ramp is steep and smooth.

questions.question: A ramp of 10 degrees was read as:
questions.explanation: The slope of the plane through the 3 by 3 cells.

questions.question: The reference vehicle's slope limit on gravel was:
options: 22.3 degrees, the smaller of the motors, the grip and the balance

questions.question: A slope of 24 degrees on gravel had a cost of:
Why does the cost rise with the square of the share of the limit?
options: It is nearly free for most of the range and steep near the limit
questions.explanation: Spend caution where the danger is.

questions.question: Why can a tall vehicle be limited by its balance and not its grip?
options: It tips at atan(half the track over the height of its centre of mass), which falls as it gets taller
questions.explanation: The limit is the smallest of three.
